cells.tense: You are at the doorway with the pen, and you already know what stays.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Name a feeling you have been carrying past its usefulness, say what it did for you, and put it down this week without asking anyone to agree.
cells.core:
You have a clear sense of what is yours to carry and what is not. Where you decide what gets let go of from something you care for, the deciding comes easy, and the people near you get the plain version. You are at the doorway with the pen and you know which things stay.

That fairness runs well one direction. Something you had to feel this year — you can say what it cost without a long argument about whether it really counted. Name a feeling you have been carrying past its usefulness. Say what it did for you, then put it down, on a weekday, without needing anyone to agree it was time. What you keep will be the truer thing.
cells.sheetLine: You know what is yours to carry, and you say it plainly.
cells.verb: decides what to keep and what to let go so the kept thing can grow
cells.place: at the doorway where what has finished its work is let go, on purpose

cells.tense: The release keeps getting rehearsed as a version that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: Next time someone tells you something they feel, take it in and keep quiet. No repair, no useful idea, no second opinion.
cells.core:
The letting-go is happening, but none of it is landing. You are already holding the next version of what you mean to release, and you have been running an ending you set down already, trying it on as if it were the one that would close the loop. The same loop gets run again. The grip does not loosen. It just gets better organized.

You keep standing in for the whole thing, and the whole thing is not workable this way. There is one move that actually moves it. Next time someone tells you something they feel, take it in and hold it without repairing a thing. Not even a useful idea. Standing next to a person instead of fixing them is how a hand comes off a doorframe. Try that before you go back to the doorway.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding the next version before this one has ended.

cells.tense: A door closed that you never stepped through, and your hand is still on it.
cells.act: keep the motivation warm with steady care
cells.ask: Find something you care about that has nothing to do with that ending. Give it real attention this week, without needing it to become anything.
cells.core:
There is a place you released, or had released out from under you, and your hand has been on it since, so the space it was supposed to open stayed shut. You are not holding on deliberately. You just haven't let the ending be true. When release is working, you can walk out of a finished thing and leave the room as it was.

Standing at a closed door turns out to be exhausting. Feed something instead — anything you care about that has nothing to do with that ending. Real attention, a little at a time, the way you'd keep a fire, without needing it to become anything. Wanting does the presence work. You just forgot it could.

cells.tense: You keep deciding what leaves and what stays, and you keep calling it circumstance.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: Set a boundary at the place where you keep describing a choice as just how things went, then hold it through one full conversation.
cells.core:
You keep making the keep-or-release call, and you keep filing it under circumstance. You describe it as the way a job went, the way a friendship wound down and nothing more. You decide what leaves and what stays, and you keep a hand in it even after you say you're finished. The call gets made. It doesn't get carried as yours.

What holds around you is something you built, and it holds because you are the one holding it. So sign the work. Notice where you file a decision under just how things went, and set a boundary at exactly that place — one line you keep in one conversation, held. You don't have to announce a pattern. Just stop letting the call be anonymous.
